examples.ko: 우리 동네에 좀도둑이 자주 든다는 소문이 있어요.
examples.en: There's a rumor that petty thieves often break in around our neighborhood.
We caught a petty thief in our shop yesterday.
I put a camera at the front door because of petty thieves.

examples.ko: 그는 큰 범인이 아니라 좀도둑일 뿐이에요.
examples.en: He's not a big criminal, just a petty thief.

examples.ko: 시장에는 좀도둑 조심하라는 안내문이 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: There are signs at the market warning about petty thieves.
Don't sneak into the fridge like a thief.

explain: '도둑'보다 작은 물건을 몰래 조금씩 훔치는 사람을 가리켜요. 가방이나 주머니에서 훔치는 '소매치기'와는 달라요. 가족끼리는 몰래 간식을 먹는 사람에게 농담으로 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It points to someone who secretly steals small things bit by bit, which makes it smaller than a plain '도둑'. It differs from '소매치기', who steals from pockets or bags. Family members sometimes use it jokingly for someone sneaking snacks.

examples.en: Our first home as newlyweds was a tiny studio.

examples.ko: 좁디좁은 골목에 차가 들어와서 길이 막혔어요.
examples.en: A car came into the very narrow alley and blocked the road.

examples.ko: 방이 좁디좁아서 책상을 놓을 데가 없어요.
examples.en: The room is so tiny that there's no place for a desk.

examples.ko: 이 버스 자리는 키 큰 사람에게 좁디좁아요.
examples.en: This bus seat is really cramped for tall people.

examples.ko: 그 집 화장실은 좁디좁다고 친구가 말했어요.
examples.en: My friend said that house's bathroom is tiny.
The very narrow road was widened, so it's more convenient now.

explain: '좁다'를 더 세게 말하고 싶을 때 써요. '넓디넓다', '높디높다'처럼 같은 말을 되풀이해서 강조하는 모양이에요. 반대는 '넓디넓다'예요.
explain_en: Use it when you want to say '좁다' (narrow) much more strongly. It repeats the adjective for emphasis, like '넓디넓다' and '높디높다'. Its opposite is '넓디넓다'.

examples.en: My grandmother made porridge out of millet for me.
Millet grains are much smaller than rice grains.
I bought a bag of millet at the market.
Try adding a little millet to your multigrain rice.
A pimple as small as a grain of millet appeared on my forehead.
Tiny grains like millet were scattered on the floor.

explain: 곡식 이름이지만 '아주 작은 것'을 비유할 때도 자주 써요. 얼굴에 난 작은 여드름을 '좁쌀 여드름'이라고도 해요. 쌀과 섞어 잡곡밥으로 많이 먹어요.

phrases.example: 우리 팀장님은 사소한 것까지 따지는 좁쌀영감이에요.
phrases.en: Our team leader is a nitpicker who argues over even trivial things.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이 좁고 자잘한 일까지 따지는 사람을 놀리듯 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A teasing name for someone petty who fusses over small details.

explain_en: It is a grain, but people also use it to describe something very tiny. Small pimples on the face are called '좁쌀 여드름'. It is often mixed with rice in multigrain rice.

examples.en: Relatives gather at the head family's house every holiday.
The eldest daughter-in-law of the head family is busy preparing for the memorial rites.
My grandfather's house is the head family's house.
The kimchi from the head family's house has a really deep flavor.
He grew up as the eldest grandson of the head family.

examples.ko: 종갓집에서 온 간장이라 더 귀하게 느껴져요.
examples.en: It's soy sauce from a head family's house, so it feels more precious.

explain: 집안의 맏이로 대를 이어 온 집을 말해요. '큰집'과 비슷하지만 종갓집은 조상 제사를 이어서 모시는 본가라는 느낌이 강해요. '종가'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is the house of the eldest line that has carried the family on through generations. It is close to '큰집', but '종갓집' strongly suggests the main house that keeps up the ancestral rites. It can also be shortened to '종가'.

examples.en: Next Friday is the last class of the semester.

examples.ko: 종강 파티는 학교 앞 식당에서 해요.
examples.en: The end-of-semester party is at a restaurant in front of school.
I'm going to start a part-time job after the semester ends.
There are still two weeks left until the end of the semester.
Just before the end of the semester, I said goodbye to my professor.
The exam results came out on the last day of class.

explain: 반대말은 '개강'이에요. 주로 대학에서 쓰고, 초·중·고등학교에서는 '방학식'이나 '종업식'이라고 해요. '종강 파티'처럼 학기가 끝난 기분을 나누는 말과 함께 많이 써요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '개강' (start of the semester). It is mostly used for universities; schools below that say '방학식' or '종업식'. It often appears in phrases like '종강 파티' (end-of-semester party).

en: to end a semester; to finish the course

examples.en: Our class ends next week.
The professor finished the course with today's class.
When the semester ends, the library becomes quiet.
When did your classes end that you're so free?
The day the course ends is different for each subject.
Some lectures ended early.

explain: 반대말은 '개강하다'예요. 주어로 '수업, 강의, 학교, 교수님'이 자연스럽게 와요. 학기의 마지막 수업이 끝났을 때 쓰는 말이라서 하루 수업이 끝나는 것에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '개강하다'. Natural subjects are a class, a lecture, a school or a professor. It means the last class of the term is over, so it isn't used for a single day's lesson ending.

examples.en: Religious leaders gathered for the sake of peace.
The religious community is also taking the lead in protecting the environment.

examples.ko: 이번 일에 대해 종교계의 반응이 엇갈렸어요.
examples.en: Reactions from the religious community were mixed about this matter.
The news reported on the religious community.
He has been involved in religious circles for a long time.
The religious community and political circles exchanged opinions.

explain: '정치계, 법조계, 학계, 재계'처럼 '-계'가 붙어 어떤 분야의 사람들 전체를 말해요. 뉴스나 글에서 많이 나오고, 개인의 믿음을 말할 때는 '종교'를 써요.
explain_en: Like '정치계', '법조계', '학계' and '재계', the '-계' ending refers to everyone in a field as a group. It is common in news and writing. For a person's own belief, use '종교' instead.

examples.ko: 쓰레기 종량제 봉투를 사러 마트에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the mart to buy trash bags for the pay-per-volume system.

examples.ko: 우리 동네는 음식물 쓰레기도 종량제로 버려요.
examples.en: In our neighborhood, food waste is also thrown away under the pay-per-volume system.
We've run out of designated trash bags at home.
After the pay-per-volume system started, the amount of trash went down.
Do the nearby convenience stores sell the designated trash bags too?

examples.ko: 종량제 실시 이후 분리배출을 더 열심히 해요.
examples.en: Since the system started, I sort my recycling more carefully.

explain: 일상에서는 거의 '쓰레기 종량제'나 '종량제 봉투'로 들어요. 버리는 양만큼 돈을 내는 제도라서, 지역에서 정한 봉투를 사서 써야 해요. 봉투 값이 지역마다 달라요.
explain_en: In daily life you mostly hear it as '쓰레기 종량제' or '종량제 봉투'. You pay according to how much you throw away, so you must buy the bags designated by your area. Bag prices differ by region.

examples.ko: 담임 선생님이 종례 시간에 공지를 하셨어요.
examples.en: The homeroom teacher made an announcement during the end-of-day meeting.
The end-of-day meeting ran long, so I missed the bus.

examples.ko: 오늘은 종례 없이 바로 집에 가요.
examples.en: Today we go straight home without the end-of-day meeting.
The teacher kept the end-of-day meeting short.
After the end-of-day meeting, the students on cleaning duty stay behind.
They call attendance at the morning and end-of-day meetings.

explain: 아침에 하는 '조례'와 짝이에요. 초·중·고등학교에서 담임 선생님이 하루 수업을 마치고 전달 사항을 말하는 시간이고, 대학에는 보통 없어요.
explain_en: It pairs with '조례', the morning meeting. In elementary, middle and high school it is the time when the homeroom teacher gives notices after the day's classes. Universities usually don't have it.

examples.ko: 둘의 점수 차이는 종잇장 두께밖에 안 돼요.
examples.en: The score difference between the two is only as thick as a sheet of paper.
Her face was white as a sheet of paper.
The walls of this house are as thin as paper.
Sheets of paper are scattered on the desk.
There isn't a gap big enough for a sheet of paper.
When I opened the window, a sheet of paper blew away in the wind.

explain: '종이'는 재료나 물건 전체를 말하고, '종잇장'은 낱장으로 된 종이 한 장을 말해요. 아주 얇은 것, 창백한 얼굴, 아주 작은 차이를 비유할 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: '종이' is paper in general, while '종잇장' is a single sheet. It is often used in comparisons for something very thin, a pale face, or a tiny difference.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 좌식이라서 신발을 벗어야 해요.
examples.en: This restaurant has floor seating, so you have to take off your shoes.
Is a floor table more uncomfortable than a chair-height one?

examples.ko: 우리 집 거실에는 좌식 책상을 놓았어요.
examples.en: We put a floor desk in our living room.
My back hurts, so living at floor level is hard.

examples.ko: 좌식과 입식 중에 어느 쪽이 좋으세요?
examples.en: Which do you prefer, floor seating or chair seating?

examples.ko: 한옥 카페는 대부분 좌식으로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: Most hanok cafés have floor seating.

explain: 반대말은 '입식'이에요. 식당을 예약할 때 '좌식으로 할까요, 입식으로 할까요?'처럼 자주 물어봐요. 의자 없이 바닥에 앉는 방식을 말해요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '입식'. When booking a restaurant you often hear a question like '좌식으로 할까요, 입식으로 할까요?'. It refers to sitting on the floor without chairs.

examples.en: There's a saying that you can't live well after doing wrong.
I feel uneasy all the time, like someone who has done wrong.
Don't commit sins; live a good life.

examples.ko: 우리 아이가 뭘 죄지었다고 그렇게 혼내세요?
examples.en: What wrong did my child do that you scold him like that?

examples.ko: 남에게 죄지으면 잠도 잘 안 와요.
examples.en: If you wrong someone, you can't sleep well either.
He did wrong and is still shameless.

explain: '죄를 짓다'처럼 '를'을 넣어서 말하기도 해요. 'ㅅ' 불규칙이라서 '죄지어요, 죄지은'처럼 'ㅅ'이 빠져요. 법적인 죄뿐 아니라 남에게 잘못한 일에도 써요.
explain_en: People also say it with the particle, as in '죄를 짓다'. It is a 'ㅅ'-irregular verb, so the 'ㅅ' drops in forms like '죄지어요' and '죄지은'. It covers not only legal crimes but also wrongs done to others.

en: penalty for a crime; price paid for wrongdoing

examples.ko: 그는 자기 죗값을 달게 받겠다고 했어요.
examples.en: He said he would gladly accept the punishment for his crime.
You're bound to pay for your wrongdoing.
It's fair to be punished as much as your crime deserves.
An apology alone doesn't wipe out the price of the crime.
The court gave a ruling that fits the crime.

examples.ko: 큰 죗값을 치른 뒤에야 그는 반성했어요.
examples.en: Only after paying a heavy price for his crime did he reflect.

explain: '죗값을 치르다', '죗값을 받다', '죗값을 달게 받다'처럼 짝으로 많이 써요. 잘못한 일에 대해 받는 벌이나 대가를 말하고, 영어 'price'처럼 물건 값을 뜻하지는 않아요.
explain_en: It appears in set phrases like '죗값을 치르다', '죗값을 받다' and '죗값을 달게 받다'. It means the punishment or consequence you receive for wrongdoing. Unlike the English 'price', it never means the cost of goods.

examples.en: Please mix the rice evenly with the paddle.
A rice paddle is hanging next to the rice cooker.

examples.ko: 주걱에 붙은 밥알이 잘 안 떨어져요.
examples.en: The rice grains stuck to the paddle don't come off easily.
A wooden paddle feels better in the hand than a plastic one.

examples.ko: 밥을 푼 뒤에는 주걱을 물에 담가 두세요.
examples.en: After serving the rice, leave the paddle soaking in water.
We only need to buy one new rice paddle.

explain: 밥을 풀 때 쓰는 도구예요. 국을 뜨는 것은 '국자', 부침개 같은 것을 뒤집는 것은 '뒤집개'라고 해서 구별해요.
explain_en: It is the tool for scooping and serving rice. A soup ladle is a '국자' and a spatula for flipping pancakes is a '뒤집개', so they are kept separate.

examples.en: This exam has a lot of open-ended questions.

examples.ko: 주관식은 답을 직접 써야 해서 어려워요.
examples.en: Open-ended questions are hard because you have to write the answer yourself.
It's harder to get points on open-ended questions than multiple-choice ones.

examples.ko: 주관식으로 답을 쓸 때는 글씨를 또박또박 써요.
examples.en: When I answer open-ended questions, I write clearly.
The last two questions are open-ended.
The teacher grades open-ended answers by hand.

explain: 반대말은 '객관식'이에요. 보기 중에서 고르지 않고 답을 직접 쓰는 문제를 말해요. 짧게 쓰는 '단답형', 길게 쓰는 '서술형'도 모두 주관식에 들어가요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '객관식' (multiple choice). It refers to questions where you write the answer yourself instead of choosing. Both short-answer '단답형' and essay-style '서술형' count as 주관식.

examples.en: It's good to get a health checkup regularly.

examples.ko: 주기적인 운동이 스트레스 해소에 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Regular exercise helps relieve stress.

examples.ko: 이 병은 주기적이라서 한동안 괜찮다가 다시 아파요.
examples.en: This illness is cyclical, so I feel fine for a while and then get sick again.
Waves roll in at regular intervals.
Payday comes around regularly every month.
The app sends notifications periodically.

explain: '정기적'과 비슷하지만 '정기적'은 날짜를 정해 두고 하는 모임이나 검사에 잘 어울리고, '주기적'은 일정한 간격으로 되풀이되는 것에 어울려요. 보통 '주기적인, 주기적으로' 모양으로 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '정기적', but '정기적' fits meetings or checkups held on set dates, while '주기적' fits things that repeat at steady intervals. It is mostly used as '주기적인' or '주기적으로'.

en: hanging in clusters; dangling in abundance

examples.en: This year every fruit tree is heavy with fruit.

examples.ko: 포도가 주렁주렁 달린 모습이 정말 풍성해요.
examples.en: The sight of grapes hanging in bunches looks really abundant.
She carries a bag with lots of dolls dangling from it.

examples.ko: 크리스마스 트리에 장식이 주렁주렁 걸려 있어요.
examples.en: Decorations hang all over the Christmas tree.
Persimmons hang in clusters on the persimmon tree.
If you pile on necklaces, it actually looks awkward.

explain: 열매나 장식 같은 것이 많이 매달려 있는 모양을 말해요. '대롱대롱'은 한두 개가 가볍게 매달린 모양이라 느낌이 달라요.
explain_en: It describes many things such as fruit or decorations hanging down together. '대롱대롱' is different, since it describes one or a few things dangling lightly.

examples.en: Grandma's hands are covered in wrinkles, but they're warm.
I left the clothes crumpled, so they're full of creases.
I ironed the wrinkled shirt and wore it.
The old map is so wrinkled that it's hard even to unfold.
A wrinkled face was full of smiles.
I put the paper in my bag and it ended up covered in creases.

explain: '-투성이'는 '온통 그것이 묻거나 가득하다'는 느낌으로, '먼지투성이, 땀투성이, 상처투성이'처럼 써요. 사람 얼굴에는 놀리는 느낌이 날 수 있어서 조심해야 해요.
explain_en: The suffix '-투성이' gives a feel of being covered or full of something, as in '먼지투성이', '땀투성이' and '상처투성이'. Used about a person's face it can sound teasing, so be careful.

examples.en: Please write your name and address on the order form.
I checked the order form and packed the goods.
The order form came in wrong, so I sent it back.
We accept group order forms by email.

examples.ko: 주문서를 보내 주시면 배송을 확인해 드려요.
examples.en: If you send me the order form, I'll check the delivery for you.

examples.ko: 식당 직원이 주문서를 들고 주방으로 갔어요.
examples.en: The restaurant staff took the order slip to the kitchen.

explain: '주문'은 시키는 행동이고, '주문서'는 그 내용을 적은 종이나 양식이에요. 돈을 낸 증거인 '영수증'과는 달라요.
explain_en: '주문' is the act of ordering, while '주문서' is the paper or form that lists what was ordered. It differs from a '영수증' (receipt), which proves payment.

examples.en: The nurse filled the syringe with the injection medicine.
This injection medicine has to be kept in the fridge.

examples.ko: 주사약이 몸에 들어갈 때 조금 따끔했어요.
examples.en: It stung a little when the injection medicine went into my body.
I was prescribed an injection medicine at the hospital because of a cold.

examples.ko: 주사약 때문에 알레르기가 생길 수도 있어요.
examples.en: An allergy can develop because of injection medicine.

examples.ko: 주사약 병은 흔들지 말고 천천히 돌려 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't shake the injection medicine bottle; roll it slowly.

explain: 먹는 약과 구별해서 몸에 주사로 넣는 약을 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '주사를 맞다'라고 하는 경우가 많고, '주사약'은 약 자체를 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It separates medicine given by injection from medicine you swallow. In everyday talk people often just say '주사를 맞다' (get a shot), and '주사약' is used when talking about the medicine itself.

examples.en: I get scared just by looking at an injection needle.
It stings when the needle goes into my arm.

examples.ko: 새 주삿바늘은 한 번만 쓰고 버려요.
examples.en: A new needle is used once and thrown away.
The child burst into tears because of the needle.
The nurse carefully took out the needle.
Be careful not to get pricked by the needle.

explain: '주사'와 '바늘' 사이에 사이시옷이 들어가서 '주삿바늘'이라고 써요. 주사를 맞을 때 몸에 들어가는 가는 바늘 부분을 말해요.
explain_en: A linking 'ㅅ' (사이시옷) is added between '주사' and '바늘', so it is written '주삿바늘'. It refers to the thin needle part that goes into the body during an injection.

en: slowly gathering things bit by bit

examples.ko: 주섬주섬 옷을 챙겨 입고 집을 나섰어요.
examples.en: I slowly gathered my clothes, put them on and left the house.
The child picked up the toys on the floor one by one.
He fumbled coins out of his pocket one after another.

examples.ko: 수업이 끝나자 학생들이 가방을 주섬주섬 쌌어요.
examples.en: When class ended, the students packed their bags bit by bit.
Grandmother slowly took in the laundry from the yard.
He tidied up his things bit by bit and stood up.

explain: 흩어진 물건을 하나씩 천천히 챙기는 모양이에요. 급해서 서두르는 '허둥지둥'과 달리 차분하고 느릿한 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It describes gathering scattered things one at a time, slowly. Unlike '허둥지둥', which is hurried and flustered, it feels calm and unhurried.

en: pick up by overhearing; hear secondhand

examples.en: I only picked up this information from a friend, so I'm not sure.
I picked up guitar by listening in from the sidelines.
I overheard that rumor while passing by.

examples.ko: 그냥 주워들어서 아는 건데 아마 맞을 거예요.
examples.en: I only know it from hearing it around, but it's probably right.

examples.ko: 어디서 주워들었는지 아이가 어려운 말을 해요.
examples.en: I don't know where he picked it up, but the child uses difficult words.
He has a habit of eavesdropping on other people's talk.

explain: 직접 배우거나 확인한 게 아니라 여기저기서 우연히 들어서 알게 된 것에 써요. '귀동냥'과 비슷하고, 정확하지 않다는 느낌이 조금 있어요. 'ㄷ' 불규칙이라서 '주워들어요, 주워들은'이 돼요.
explain_en: Use it for things you learned by overhearing here and there rather than studying or checking them. It is close to '귀동냥' and carries a slight sense that the knowledge may not be accurate. It is a 'ㄷ'-irregular verb: '주워들어요', '주워들은'.

examples.en: The main cause of this accident was drowsy driving.

examples.ko: 이 병의 주원인을 아직 찾지 못했어요.
examples.en: We haven't found the main cause of this illness yet.
Oversleeping is the main reason I'm late.
Experts point to lack of sleep as the main cause.
Let's first find out what the main cause is.
The investigation into the main cause of the fire is over.

explain: 여러 원인 중 가장 중요한 원인을 말해요. 일상에서는 '이유'라고 많이 하고, '주원인'은 사고·병·문제를 설명하는 뉴스나 보고서에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means the most important cause among several. In daily talk people say '이유' more, while '주원인' often appears in news and reports that explain accidents, illnesses or problems.

examples.ko: 식당 주인장이 직접 서비스를 챙겨 줬어요.
examples.en: The restaurant owner personally gave us extra treats.

examples.ko: 주인장님, 여기 물 좀 더 주세요.
examples.en: Boss, could we have some more water here?

examples.ko: 이 가게 주인장은 손님 이름을 다 외워요.
examples.en: The owner of this shop remembers all the customers' names.
I ordered the owner's recommended dish.

examples.ko: 카페 주인장과 이야기를 나누다 보니 시간이 훌쩍 갔어요.
examples.en: Chatting with the café owner, time flew by.

examples.ko: 주인장께서 오늘은 일찍 문을 닫는다고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The owner said they'll close early today.

explain: 가게, 식당, 숙소 같은 곳의 주인을 친근하게 부르는 말이에요. 손님이 부를 때는 보통 '사장님'이라고 하고, '주인장'은 조금 정감 있고 예스러운 느낌이에요. 블로그나 모임의 주인을 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is a friendly way to refer to the owner of a shop, restaurant or lodging. Customers usually call them '사장님'; '주인장' feels a bit warmer and old-fashioned. It can also refer to the owner of a blog or a gathering.

examples.en: I burst out laughing at the wrong moment during the meeting.

examples.ko: 그는 주책없이 아무 데서나 큰소리로 떠들어요.
examples.en: He chatters loudly anywhere without any sense of propriety.

examples.ko: 주책없이 눈물이 나서 얼른 고개를 돌렸어요.
examples.en: Tears came at the wrong time, so I quickly turned my head away.
Don't butt into other people's conversations thoughtlessly.

examples.ko: 나이 들어서 주책없이 이런 말을 해서 미안해요.
examples.en: I'm sorry for saying this at my age, it's a bit out of place.

examples.ko: 심장이 주책없이 뛰어서 말을 못 하겠어요.
examples.en: My heart is pounding so hard that I can't speak.

explain: 말이나 행동이 경솔하고 분위기에 맞지 않을 때 써요. 내 눈물이나 웃음, 심장처럼 마음대로 안 되는 것이 때에 맞지 않게 나올 때도 '주책없이'라고 해요. '철없이'와 비슷하지만 때와 장소에 안 맞는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: Use it when words or actions are careless and don't fit the mood. It is also used when something you can't control, like tears, laughter or a heartbeat, shows up at the wrong time. It is close to '철없이', but with a stronger sense of being out of place.

examples.ko: 주체적인 사람은 남의 눈치를 덜 봐요.
examples.en: Independent people worry less about what others think.
I want to live my own life on my own terms.

examples.ko: 선택을 남에게 맡기면 주체적일 수 없어요.
examples.en: If you leave your choices to others, you can't be self-directed.

examples.ko: 주체적인 태도가 면접에서 좋은 인상을 줘요.
examples.en: A self-driven attitude makes a good impression in interviews.

examples.ko: 어른이 되면 주체적으로 결정할 일이 많아요.
examples.en: When you become an adult, there are many things to decide on your own.
I feel good when I'm told I'm self-directed.

explain: 남에게 끌려가지 않고 스스로 판단하고 행동한다는 느낌이에요. '자주적'은 나라나 단체가 스스로 서는 것에 더 잘 쓰고, '능동적'은 적극적으로 움직이는 것에 써요.
explain_en: It gives the feel of judging and acting by yourself instead of being led by others. '자주적' fits a country or organization standing on its own, and '능동적' fits actively taking action.

examples.en: Because of the housing shortage, home prices are high in big cities.

examples.ko: 주택난이 심해서 신혼부부가 집 구하기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The housing shortage is severe, so newlyweds struggle to find a home.

examples.ko: 정부가 주택난을 해결하려고 새 아파트를 지어요.
examples.en: The government is building new apartments to solve the housing shortage.
Even amid the housing shortage, monthly rent keeps rising.
That city has suffered from a housing shortage for a long time.
The housing shortage is a big worry for young people.

explain: '-난(難)'이 붙으면 '구하기 어려운 어려움'을 뜻해서 '취업난, 구인난, 식량난'처럼 써요. 주로 뉴스나 사회 이야기에서 나와요.
explain_en: The suffix '-난(難)' means difficulty in obtaining something, as in '취업난', '구인난' and '식량난'. This word mostly appears in news and discussions of social issues.

examples.ko: 요리는 제 주특기라고 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You could say cooking is my specialty.
That player's specialty is quick dribbling.

examples.ko: 면접에서 제 주특기를 살려서 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: In the interview, I showed off my specialty.
Telling jokes has become Dad's specialty.
I'll make you my specialty, rolled omelet.
This time I'm going to compete with my best skill.

explain: '특기'보다 '가장 자신 있는 것'이라는 느낌이 강해요. 친구끼리는 농담처럼 '그건 내 주특기지!'라고도 해요. 군대에서는 맡은 일의 종류를 '주특기'라고 부르기도 해요.
explain_en: Compared with '특기', it has a stronger sense of 'the thing I'm most confident at'. Friends also say it jokingly, like '그건 내 주특기지!'. In the military, '주특기' is also the name for a soldier's assigned job type.

examples.en: My grandfather calculated quickly with an abacus.
I saw an old abacus at the museum.
You move the abacus beads up and down with your fingers.
These days people use calculators instead of abacuses.
Do you know what an abacus looks like?
I still remember the sound of my mother's abacus.

explain: 구슬을 움직여서 계산하는 옛날 도구예요. 요즘은 계산기가 흔해서 일상에서는 거의 안 쓰고, 아래 표현처럼 비유로 더 자주 들어요.

phrases.example: 그는 손해와 이익을 따지며 주판을 튕기고 있어요.
phrases.en: He is weighing losses and gains, calculating carefully.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이익과 손해를 이리저리 계산해 본다는 뜻이에요. 조금 속셈이 있는 느낌으로 쓰기도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means weighing profit against loss. It can carry a slight sense of having an ulterior motive.
phrases.en_equiv: run the numbers; calculate the angles

explain_en: It is an old tool for calculating by moving beads. Calculators are common now, so it is rarely used in daily life, and you more often hear it in figurative phrases like the one below.

examples.ko: 창밖에 황혼이 내려앉자 방 안이 주홍빛으로 물들었어요.
examples.en: When dusk settled outside the window, the room was tinted a vermilion glow.
The tree is full of reddish-orange persimmons.

examples.ko: 그 화가는 주홍과 파랑을 즐겨 써요.
examples.en: That painter likes to use vermilion and blue.
The sunset in the western sky spread in a vermilion color.
The evening sky changed from vermilion to purple.
Vermilion lanterns lit up the alley.

explain: 붉은 기가 도는 주황색을 말해요. '주황'은 오렌지색이고 '주홍'은 그보다 붉은 느낌이 더 강해요. '주홍빛, 주홍색'처럼 뒤에 붙여서 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is an orange with a red tint. '주황' is plain orange, while '주홍' leans redder. It is often used with a suffix, as in '주홍빛' or '주홍색'.

examples.en: In spring I went to the mountain to dig up bamboo shoots.
The stir-fried bamboo shoots are crunchy and tasty.

examples.ko: 비가 온 뒤 죽순이 쑥쑥 자랐어요.
examples.en: After the rain, the bamboo shoots grew rapidly.
Bamboo shoots often go into Chinese dishes.
I bought boiled bamboo shoots at the mart.
You peel bamboo shoots before cooking them.

explain: 대나무의 어린 싹을 먹는 재료예요. 비 온 뒤 죽순처럼 빨리 자란다고 해서 '우후죽순'이라는 말도 있어요. 아삭한 식감이 특징이에요.
explain_en: It is a food ingredient, the young shoot of bamboo. Because shoots grow quickly after rain, there is also the four-character expression '우후죽순'. Its crunchy texture is a key feature.

examples.ko: 사장이 시키는 대로 하느라 직원들만 죽어나요.
examples.en: Only the employees suffer, doing whatever the boss orders.

examples.ko: 일은 다 나한테 맡겨서 나만 죽어나는 거예요.
examples.en: They leave all the work to me, so I'm the only one who suffers.
They say the accounting team has a terrible time at year-end.
Every time the boss changed, only the staff below suffered.
You'll have a miserable time in this heat without air conditioning.
When adults fight, it's always the kids who suffer.

explain: 남의 일이나 상황 때문에 억울하게 고생할 때 쓰는 말이에요. '나만 죽어나다', '아랫사람만 죽어난다'처럼 '~만'과 함께 많이 써요. 일상에서는 불평하는 말투로 많이 들려요.
explain_en: It is used when someone has a hard time unfairly because of other people or circumstances. It often pairs with '~만', as in '나만 죽어나다' or '아랫사람만 죽어난다'. In daily life it usually comes out as a complaint.
